system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s assertions that positions are “standard”, “final” or agreed should not be accepted without confirmation from the Buyer deal team. Review of the full SPA and underlying DD documents remains necessary.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price / AUD 4.8m**. | At least **50% of price / AUD 12m** for general warranties, with separate higher caps for title, tax, IP and specific indemnities; assess escrow/W&I support. | **Reject 20% and counter at 50%** — AUD 4.8m may be inadequate for correlated SaaS, customer, privacy and IP losses. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, so only excess is recoverable. | Lower de minimis (e.g. **AUD 10,000**) and a **tipping basket of AUD 120,000–150,000**, with related claims aggregated and no thresholds for special claims. | **Counter both thresholds and make the basket first-dollar** — the proposed structure suppresses legitimate claims and leaves the Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims expire **18 months after Completion**; Seller seeks to apply limitations to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties; longer periods for title, tax, IP, covenants and indemnities; timely notice should preserve a claim until resolved. | **Reject the universal 18-month limitation** — material SaaS, customer and compliance issues may not emerge within one audit cycle. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month period as general warranties. | Separate fundamental regime with a **100% purchase-price cap** and at least **six years’ survival**, unaffected by baskets or knowledge/disclosure. | **Reject** — the Buyer must have full recourse if the Seller cannot validly sell 100% of the shares. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is offered. | Express carve-outs for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful misconduct and deliberate concealment by the Seller and relevant officers/agents, preserving non-excludable statutory rights. | **Insert an overriding fraud carve-out** — a Seller must not benefit from caps, time bars or non-reliance where information was dishonestly concealed. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, registers and public records, without admitting breach, materiality or liability. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify their nature and likely scope; indexed final data-room copy and updated disclosure at Completion. | **Delete general disclosure** — bulk or constructive disclosure improperly transfers the diligence risk to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for anything known by the Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Prefer no knowledge qualification; failing that, only actual conscious knowledge of named senior Buyer individuals, proved by Seller, excluding advisers and constructive/imputed knowledge. | **Reject the proposed qualifier** — “discoverable” information could defeat warranties even where the risk was obscure or incompletely disclosed. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of the counterparty’s written consent. No final consent or proof of clause 11.3 satisfaction exists. | A genuine CP requiring unconditional written consent/waiver, satisfaction of all associated conditions, no adverse amendment or payment, and form acceptable to Buyer. | **Do not permit deemed satisfaction or waiver without Buyer consent** — Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; release is to be provided after Completion. | Repayment through controlled funds flow and executed releases/discharges of all guarantees and security delivered at or simultaneously with Completion. | **Make discharge a Completion deliverable** — a post-Completion promise conflicts with the debt-free acquisition and leaves the target encumbered. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are described as a Seller matter and omitted from funds flow; on-costs are unspecified. | Seller to bear the bonuses plus payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs through funds flow, price/debt adjustment or a specific indemnity. | **Expressly allocate and quantify the liability** — Completion triggers a target-company cost that otherwise economically falls on the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment issue; AUD 180,000 remains recorded as open and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is provided. | Pre-Completion payment, written confirmation/assignment of all Project Materials, and a broad indemnity for loss arising from deficient ownership, transfer or use rights. | **Expand the indemnity and require title evidence** — paying only the invoice does not establish that critical IP has validly vested in the Company. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Incident characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain undetermined. | Prompt forensic investigation and containment, regulator/affected-person analysis, Completion update, warranties and a specific indemnity for investigation, remediation, notification, claims and penalties where lawfully recoverable. | **Treat as a known special risk, not general disclosure** — the possible export of 1,240 records creates unresolved privacy, security and reputational exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals are said to be ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure does not establish timing, termination, accrual or avoidability. | Contracts and invoices, renewal/termination rights, accounting treatment and evidence of authority; Seller bears pre-Completion or unauthorised commitments, with appropriate working-capital/debt treatment. | **Do not accept the ordinary-course label without evidence** — the AUD 330,000 aggregate commitment may be accrued, avoidable or outside normal trading. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Limitations and exclusive-remedy provisions apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | Expressly separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, debt/leakage, Completion obligations, covenants, fraud and preserved statutory claims. | **Rewrite the limitations architecture** — a global limitation can unintentionally cap or extinguish the Buyer’s most important protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Seller relies on the Company share register at DD-012 as evidence that it holds 100% of the shares. | Original/current register and certificates, constitution and issuance/transfer records, ASIC and PPSR searches, cap-table reconciliation, absence of options or third-party rights, and Completion transfers. | **Require independent corroboration and full title warranties** — a company-maintained register alone does not eliminate competing beneficial, security or issuance claims. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties are treated as settled under the 20% cap, thresholds and 18-month general regime. | A tax covenant/indemnity surviving through the applicable assessment period plus a buffer (customarily up to seven years), and enhanced IP warranties/indemnities with materially higher caps and longer survival. | **Keep tax and IP outside the general regime** — historic tax liabilities and defective core-software ownership can exceed the general cap and emerge late. |

### Immediate Buyer priorities

1. Make **Bluefen consent** and **Riverlark discharge** hard Completion conditions/deliverables.  
2. Allocate the **AUD 420,000 bonuses and on-costs** to Seller.  
3. Resolve **Ironquay IP ownership** before Completion.  
4. Obtain a completed investigation and specific protection for the **export/privacy incident**.  
5. Replace the global limitations/disclosure framework with clearly separated claim categories and express fraud protection.
=== END ADVICE ===
